body:
did you know: taylor wrote "no body, no crime" completely alone -- deep in a true-crime documentary-and-podcast phase -- then sent aaron dessner a voice memo of the whole finished thing.

the murder victim in the song is named este. as in este haim. taylor sent the track to haim and asked if este and danielle would sing on it, and they said yes immediately. the production leans all the way into its country staging, harmonica and all, and it actually went to country radio as a single in january 2021.

and when haim opened eras tour shows in 2023, "no body, no crime" bumped "'tis the damn season" to become the evermore set's opener -- este singing the song named after her own fictional death. a whole murder mystery, cheating husband and framed mistress and a sister for an alibi, tucked into the quietest, woodsiest album she's made.

evermore really was a villain arc in a cabin.

longlivets.com
why: Did-you-know track-fact pillar on a cold era: evermore has had zero coverage in recent posted/ or queue/ (recent posts skew Speak Now, 1989, Debut, folklore, showgirl), so it's the thinnest-covered corner, and no exact Aug-5 on-this-day Vault match exists for today. Every claim traces to the vault evermore item 'no body, no crime, a murder ballad with HAIM' (Wikipedia + Rolling Stone/Aaron Dessner interview sourced): the song written entirely alone during a true-crime doc/podcast phase, sent to Dessner as a finished voice memo; the victim named Este after Este Haim; Taylor sending HAIM the track and them saying yes immediately; the country-radio single release Jan 2021; and HAIM opening 2023 Eras shows with it, bumping "'tis the damn season" as the evermore set opener. Song-lore only -- the 'murder' is the track's fictional narrative, outside every #36/Clownbot blocklist topic (no real legal wrongdoing, health, or private-life content).
